items.title: Node keeps user-private value in spirit/run/relay-state: Email
items.box:
Node keeps user-private value in spirit/run/relay-state: Email (goal/G26.1)

Andy, 2026-10-14: "A node-global value "emailAddress" will be stored in spirit/run/relay-state/, the users email address,"
Andy, 2026-10-14: "The node needs a new verb in the loopBack API: emailAdress, where in the api does it belong?"
Andy, 2026-10-14: "The email address will be maintained in, and an be changed in the shell-app called "info""
Andy, 2026-10-14: "Most of the apiServers plugins will depend on knowing the users email."
Andy, 2026-10-14: "fill the box with what is required to maintain one node-global email address."
Andy, 2026-10-14: "the file spirit/run/js/fieldRules.js will be extended to provide validation checks for email addresses."
Andy, 2026-10-14: "the folder spirit/run/shell/js/will require a new UI element: emailAdress, that contains an element emailAddress, that all shell apps must use to show/maintain the emailAddress belonging to the node User."
Andy, 2026-10-14: "update the box appropriately."
Andy, 2026-10-14: "Q1: Should plugins get the email address at mount from apiServer, or ask apiServer for it on request?"
Andy, 2026-10-14: "the appServer module should carry the email address via the spirit Object (kernel.js) to the appServers, same way the local loopback-port of the node is carried to the appServer. same pattern."
Andy, 2026-10-14: "modify the box accordingly and cap. remove the red Q if this question has been handled."

WHAT IS REQUIRED (design, no code until Andy says go)

1. STORE. One node-global value, "emailAddress", the user's email address. File: spirit/run/relay-state/emailAddress.json, shape {"emailAddress": "<address>"}. Absent file = no address set (the ordinary first-run state; nothing is written). Written only by the node, only through the verb below. Same home as node.json and contacts.json (relay-state under rootDir), so backup.js already covers it, encrypted.

2. ONE READER. A single module owns read and write of that file (proposed: spirit/run/js/emailAddress.js, same shape as nodeSettings.js: one read per home, problems reported, never throws to a caller). Nothing else opens the file.

3. VALIDATION ON WRITE, IN fieldRules.js. spirit/run/js/fieldRules.js is extended with the email check (Andy's ruling above), so the node and every shell app use the same rule, the way labels and descriptions already do. The rule: a string, trimmed, at most 254 bytes (fieldRules counts bytes, goal/G4.16), one "@" with text on both sides and no spaces. The node enforces it on write; the browser copy is a courtesy only. Anything else is refused with ok:false and nothing changes. An empty string clears the value (back to absent).

4. THE VERB. Name in the loopBack API: node.emailAddress, one verb that reads and sets, shaped like node.debug: {} reads, {emailAddress: "<address>"} sets; both answer {ok, emailAddress} as it now stands. Placement: the "node" namespace in server.js, claimed by hub.js, next to node.setName and node.setDescription, with wire: false (local, loopback only, the node's own box). It is NOT a new namespace and NOT the owner namespace (owner.* is for puppet commands). The spelling is node.emailAddress; Andy's "emailAdress" is read as this verb (to be confirmed by Andy).

5. PRIVATE. The address is the owner's. It must never appear in node.card, in any relay post, in peerPost replies, in the trafficLog or in any other log line. node.card stays as it is. Only the owner's loopback reads it.

6. UI ELEMENT, spirit/run/shell/js/. Per Andy's ruling: a new UI element "emailAdress" in spirit/run/shell/js/ that contains an element "emailAddress". Every shell app uses this one element to show and maintain the node user's email address; no shell app draws its own. (Reading of "emailAdress" as the element name, the spelling of Andy's ruling; to be confirmed by Andy.) It validates with fieldRules and reports refusals, the same way contactLabel.js does.

7. INFO APP. The shell app "info" (spirit/run/shell/info/info.js) uses that element for its one field. It reads with node.emailAddress {} and writes with node.emailAddress {emailAddress}, the same way the name field calls node.setName through infoApi.verb. Info shows the address, says plainly when none is set, and reports a refused value.

8. FOR THE PLUGINS (Q1, answered by Andy). The appServer module carries the email address to the apiServer and its plugins via the spirit Object (kernel.js), the same way the node's local loopback-port is carried to the appServer. Same pattern. So a plugin receives the address as a value at mount, handed down from the spirit Object; it does not ask for it on request. Plugins never read relay-state and never get the database (desk.js pattern: each plugin gets its private state folder and a publish call). The file is read once at startup, and the value is carried from there; a successful node.emailAddress set updates the value the spirit Object carries. Not decided here: whether a set reaches plugins already mounted (this item adds no live push and changes no plugin).

NOT IN THIS ITEM: any plugin, the apiServer itself, any relay change, any use of the address in a message.

Box updated (v3): Q1 handled. The address reaches plugins at mount via the spirit Object (kernel.js), same as the loopback port; no on-request call. Red Q1 cleared.
Question: will the node have to reboot for the email to be updated in all appServers spirit-object?

Levant: **Short answer: no reboot of the node is needed, but the appServers do need a restart before they see a new address.**

The facts, from the code:
- `spirit/run/js/appServer.js` (lines 499-508) reads `--node` once, at process start, into `spirit.core.node.const`.
- `spirit/run/js/jobs.js` (lines 477-482) builds `--node` from `loadIdentity` and `loadOwner` when `startNodeServers` runs. Its comment says a server learns a changed owner only when the node starts it again.
- `startNodeServers` runs at node start (`server.js` 1460) and when a process is switched on (`server.js` 1924). Nothing re-sends `--node` to a running server.

So a successful `node.emailAddress` set changes only the node's own copy. Each appServer keeps the value it was started with until it is restarted.

Two things the box needs before go:
1. The box's line "a successful node.emailAddress set updates the value the spirit Object carries" is wrong for the appServer processes. It is true only for the node. I have not edited the box, since this is a question, not a ruling. Say the word and I will amend it.
2. Passing the address in `--node` puts it in the process arguments, which `ps` and some logs can show. That conflicts with rule 5 (the address must never reach a log). Andy, do you accept that, or should the address come another way, for example a file the server reads at start, or a message over its pipe?

items.title: What API-provider plugins share.
items.box:
What API-provider plugins share.

Andy, 2026-10-14 (goal/G26.3 chat), verbatim:
- API provider plugins run in the same process as the apiServer, and get access to the same spirit-object that the apiServer gets at mount time.
- before mounting provider plugins, the apiServer equips its spirit object with all common interfaces the plugins will require,
- it is at apiServer mount-time that all its plugins are "required" into the apiServers process.
- the data for the apiServers state will be a json file apiProvider.json. it must be .gitignored! it stores an object that has at its root one key per provider plugin, same name as the provider plugin, the provider plugin will store all its information via functions provided in the spirit object of the apiServer, the names/keys there will sound like "anthropic", "openai", "google", "facebook" etc...

Andy, 2026-10-14 (goal/G26.3 chat), verbatim:
every provider object in apiProvider.json is divided in to keys, marking the separate api's they provide. ( i know google has many of them)

every api has payment conditions (free, prepaid-per-unit, auto-rebill, etc) this should sensibly be reflected in the common functions related to the udating/reading of  apiProvider.json.

hierarchy
{
  google:{
     gmail:{ cost:{} }
     auth:{ cost:{}}
  },
  anthropic:{},
}

the apiServer serves the following verbs

in the

- search () returns one row for every api that matches.

Concepts, formulated from those rulings:
1. Shape: apiServer is an appServer with one plugin per API supplier. Plugins live under spirit/run/process/js/apiServer/plugin/, one per supplier: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Facebook, GitHub.
2. Pattern: as desk already has it, a plugin is the folder plugin/js/<name>/ holding <name>.js and <name>.json; no .json, no plugin. Plugins mount in name order, once, before the server serves. Each plugin is handed its own private state folder and a publish call, never the database. (The stackFrameChecks plugin under desk/plugins/js/ is the example in the tree.)
3. Same process: provider plugins run inside the apiServer process and receive the same spirit-object the apiServer receives at mount time.
4. Equip before plugins: before any provider plugin mounts, the apiServer adds to its spirit-object every common interface the plugins will require.
5. Mount-time require: all provider plugins are required into the apiServer process at apiServer mount time, and not later.
6. State: one file, apiProvider.json, which must be gitignored. Its root is an object with one key per provider plugin, the key equal to the plugin's name ("anthropic", "openai", "google", "facebook", "github"). Each plugin stores all its information only through functions the apiServer provides on the spirit-object; no plugin writes the file itself.
7. Nesting: under each provider key, one key per separate API that provider offers (google: gmail, auth, ...). Each API key holds a cost object (cost:{}). A provider with a single API is still keyed the same way (anthropic: {} until its APIs are listed).
8. Payment conditions: every API declares its payment condition (free, prepaid-per-unit, auto-rebill, etc). The common read/update functions for apiProvider.json carry that condition, so the shape of cost is set by it.
9. Verbs: the apiServer serves verbs. search () returns one row for every API that matches.

Open, not decided here: the exact names of the common interfaces; the exact fields of cost per payment condition; whether the apiProvider.json gitignore line is added by the first build item.

items.title: The apiServers shell app in the spirit group.
items.box:
apiServer: an appServer with a plugin per API supplier, plus its shell app. Both are named "apiServer" (singular).

RULINGS (Andy, verbatim, 2026-10-14)
- "this one is called apiServer, it will be an appServer with a plugin per api-supplier."
- "the appServer plugin pattern occurs already in plugins like desk. Is it enough to mention that pattern in the box, to get the idea. The folder spirit/run/process/js/apiServer/ will contain a plugin/ folder where, we already know there will be plugins for: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Facebook, GitHub."
- Q1: "the appServer name and the shell app name are both "apiServer" one lives in the shell folder, the other in the process folder."
- Q1 mount: "the mount rules for the shell app is defined by the shell, the mount rules for the appServer called "apiServer" is implied by the module spirit/run/js/appServer.js"
- Manifest: "both the shell and the server halfs of apiServer come with a co-located manifest file apiServer.json, which specifies mount-related information like / is this mounted at all / does it have a preferred icon (shell mount) / etc...."
- Manifest (2026-10-14 13:42): "Manifest fields are ruled by shell and appServer mechanisms, they contain no app-specific data/fields"
- Mount location: "that's how we'll do it." (the mount goes in spirit/run/js/appServerPlugin.js, per levant's line: "spirit/run/js/appServerPlugin.js does not exist today; only spirit/run/js/appServer.js, and it mounts no plugins. A shared appServerPlugin.js would let apiServer use the mount without touching desk.")
- State (2026-10-14 13:42): "server state is always kept in its folder, in this case its the the json file in spirit/run/process/js/apiServer/"
- Shell: "shell apps always live in spirit/run/shell/<appName>/<appName>.js ALWAYS. the shell app has the same name as the appServer process: "apiServer", this indicates clearly the coupling of shell app and appServer"
- Shell: "The shell app maintains a list of API's in a pretty looking table. with following columns: provider; api; cost scheme; fixed-cost of prepaid budget. when a user clicks on a row, a provider-specific dialog opens, which maintains at the top the common fields."
- Shell: "the dialog should open for every provider/api combination separately."
- State shape (Andy, 2026-10-14 13:44, "agreed"): "levant-local 15:43 Recommend one flat state object: { "rows": [ { "provider", "api", "costScheme", "fixedCost" or "prepaidBudget", "currency", "period", "notes", "fields": {...} } ] }. The shell table maps 1:1 onto rows; provider-specific fields (workspace, organization, seats, etc.) sit in each row's "fields" since they differ by provider."

DESIGN
- Process folder: spirit/run/process/js/apiServer/ holds apiServer.js, apiServer.json (server manifest: mount facts only), the one state JSON file (flat, shape above), and plugin/js/<name>/ with <name>.js and <name>.json for anthropic, openai, google, facebook, github. Name rule as desk's: /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,47}$/.
- Plugin contract, as desk's: no .json, no plugin. <name>.js exports function(apiServer) returning { refuses, handles, verbs }, every part optional. Each plugin's .json holds mount facts only.
- Mount: shared module spirit/run/js/appServerPlugin.js (new). Reads the plugin folder, sorts names, skips a name with no .js or unparsable .json, mounts each once before apiServer serves. apiServer uses it. desk.js and spirit/run/js/appServer.js are not changed.

Design only. No code is written under this item until Andy says go.

What the code holds today (read, not remembered):
- spirit/run/process/js/deskUnsloth/connection.json holds a key for 127.0.0.1:8888. It is tracked in git (a2786053), and the master review (design/reviews/claude-clowd/2026-10-10-master-review.md:227) says the process reads it from its state folder, so the tracked copy is dead. .gitignore:239 names the path, yet git tracks the file, so the ignore does not stop it.
- relay-state/proxy.json (spirit/run/js/proxyList.js) holds key NAMES and websites, not secrets: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to api.anthropic.com, GROK_API_KEY to api.x.ai, GROK_MANAGEMENT_KEY to management-api.x.ai (GET only). Out of scope for this item unless a removal is ruled.
- The secret values come from the environment (platform/windows/start-spirit.ps1:48-52 reads them from Machine or User settings).

Scope (Andy's ruling): only connection.json moves. deskUnsloth keeps the provider selector in its Connect tab. configuration.json is out of scope, not inventoried.

Basic procedure (capped; steps narrowed to connection.json):
1. Inventory: record the key setup in connection.json (name and location only, never the value).
2. Rotate the committed sk-unsloth- key first, since it is in a public repo. Andy does this; agents do not print or copy it.
3. Untrack connection.json from git; keep it out of the repo.
4. Move the setup into apiServer: the secret stays in the plugin's private state folder (or the environment), and the row in the apiServer dataset (goal/G26) holds only a reference to it.
5. Point deskUnsloth at apiServer for the key, and check it still reaches its website. The provider selector in the Connect tab stays.
6. Remove the old connection.json from deskUnsloth's folder. Any proxy.json entry that no longer applies is removed through the proxy verbs, not by file edit.
7. Check: a test that deskUnsloth starts with the key from apiServer and not from its own file; and that no key value appears in git, in served rows, or in chat.
8. Only then close goal/G26.

Open for Andy: whether the rotation is done before the move starts.
